sentenceSets.sentence: His bumptious self-promotion made him the least popular candidate in an otherwise competitive field.

answerChoices.reasoning: Conceited means having excessive pride in oneself; while both refer to arrogance, 'bumptious' specifically emphasizes loud, obtrusive self-assertion rather than private arrogance.
Immodest means lacking modesty; the sentence's focus on 'self-promotion' that makes him unpopular emphasizes obtrusively pushing himself forward, not just lack of modesty.

Vain refers to excessive pride in appearance or achievements; while his self-promotion may stem from vanity, 'bumptious' specifically emphasizes loud, obtrusive assertion, which is why he becomes unpopular.
Grandiose means extravagantly ambitious; while both imply excessive self-regard, 'bumptious' emphasizes the obtrusively self-assertive nature of the behavior, not just grand ambitions.
Ambitious means driven to succeed; while self-promotion suggests ambition, 'bumptious' emphasizes the presumptuous, obtrusive quality that makes him unpopular.
Overconfident means excessively sure of oneself; self-promotion reflects overconfidence, but 'bumptious' emphasizes the obtrusively aggressive manner.
Showy means ostentatiously displaying; his self-promotion is showy, but 'bumptious' emphasizes the presumptuous and noisily self-assertive quality.
Swaggering means walking or behaving with exaggerated confidence; while the sentence may suggest this, 'bumptious' emphasizes obtrusively pushing oneself forward and the resulting unpopularity.
Self-effacing means modestly withdrawing from notice; this is the opposite of the obtrusive self-promotion described in the sentence.
Unassuming means modest and not pretentious; this is opposite to the self-promotion that makes him unpopular.
Diffident means lacking confidence; this contradicts someone engaged in aggressive self-promotion.

sentenceSets.sentence: The bumptious newcomer at the party immediately launched into a loud story about his recent accomplishments, oblivious to the disinterest around him.

answerChoices.reasoning: Boastful means given to bragging; while his story shows boasting, 'bumptious' specifically emphasizes the loud, obtrusively self-assertive manner that ignores social cues.

Arrogant means having excessive pride; while the newcomer's behavior reflects arrogance, 'bumptious' emphasizes the noisily obtusive self-assertion, particularly his obliviousness to others' disinterest.
Intrusive means intruding or obtrusive; the newcomer's loud story interrupts the party atmosphere, but 'bumptious' specifically emphasizes presumptuous self-assertion, not merely being in the way.
Obnoxious means offensive and annoying; while others find him obnoxious, 'bumptious' emphasizes his presumptuous, noisily self-assertive manner as the source of that annoyance.
Brash means impulsive and tactless; the 'immediately launched' and 'loud story' show brashness, but 'bumptious' emphasizes the presumptuous self-assertion more specifically.
Bold means daring and fearless; while launching into stories shows boldness, 'bumptious' conveys presumptuous obtrusiveness rather than courage.
Aggressive means hostile or forceful; while the loud story-telling is forceful, 'bumptious' emphasizes obtrusively assuming acceptance without warrant.
Tactless means insensitive; the newcomer is tactless in missing the disinterest, but 'bumptious' emphasizes the presumptuous self-assertion that creates the insensitivity.
Modest means humble and unassuming; this directly opposes the loud self-promotion and obtrusiveness shown in the sentence.
Humble means lacking arrogance; this is opposite to someone loudly promoting his accomplishments.
Reserved means restrained and quiet; this contradicts the loud, immediately self-assertive behavior described.

sentenceSets.sentence: The bumptious executive interrupted colleagues repeatedly during the presentation, steering every discussion back to his own achievements and viewpoints.

answerChoices.reasoning: Domineering means controlling and overbearing; while the executive is domineering through interruptions, 'bumptious' emphasizes presumptuous self-assertion and obtrusiveness rather than authoritative control.
Dismissive means disregarding others' input; by interrupting and redirecting, the executive is dismissive, but 'bumptious' emphasizes the presumptuous self-assertion driving the behavior.
Self-centered means focused on oneself; steering every discussion to his achievements shows self-centeredness, but 'bumptious' emphasizes the obtrusively assertive manner of doing so.
Egotistical means excessively self-focused; while the executive is egotistical, 'bumptious' specifically emphasizes the noisily obtrusive and presumptuous quality of the assertions.
Assertive means confident and forceful; the interruptions and steering of discussion are assertive, but 'bumptious' conveys presumptuous obtrusiveness rather than mere confidence.
Opinionated means having strong views; while the executive repeatedly insists on his viewpoint, 'bumptious' emphasizes the obtrusively self-assertive manner.
Controlling means exerting power; steering the discussion reflects control, but 'bumptious' emphasizes the presumptuous, noisily self-assertive nature of the behavior.
Abrupt means sudden and sharp; while the interruptions are abrupt, 'bumptious' emphasizes the presumptuous, obtrusively self-assertive character.
Deferential means respectfully submissive; this is the opposite of repeatedly interrupting and steering discussions toward oneself.
Subordinate means lower in rank; the executive's behavior shows dominance, opposite to this.
Shy means reserved and quiet; this contradicts an executive who repeatedly interrupts and dominates discussions.
